evals.prompt: Run an OSS project health check on pgvector/pgvector — bus factor, commit and release cadence, issue response time, open security advisories — and tell me whether it is healthy, at-risk or abandoned.
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Resolves the full owner/repo slug and gathers a snapshot over a stated window; Computes the CHAOSS Contributor Absence Factor (bus factor) from commits by author, excluding bots; Reads cadence, responsiveness and advisories with the stated thresholds and calls exactly one verdict; Names the single biggest risk and writes 'data not found' for any null field; Keeps the Ecosyste.ms CC-BY-SA attribution when its numbers are quoted.
expectations: Resolves the full owner/repo slug and gathers a snapshot over a stated window
Computes the CHAOSS Contributor Absence Factor (bus factor) from commits by author, excluding bots
Reads cadence, responsiveness and advisories with the stated thresholds and calls exactly one verdict
Names the single biggest risk and writes 'data not found' for any null field
Keeps the Ecosyste.ms CC-BY-SA attribution when its numbers are quoted

evals.prompt: The last commit on this GitHub repo was eight months ago and one maintainer wrote almost all the code. Is this project dying, or is it just a finished library — should we keep depending on it?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Distinguishes a stable, feature-complete library from an abandoned one using releases and issue responsiveness, not commit count alone; Reports the bus factor as fragile when one author holds most commits; Does not call 'abandoned' unless commit, release and issue-response stalls all exceed their bars; States confidence from data completeness.
expectations: Distinguishes a stable, feature-complete library from an abandoned one using releases and issue responsiveness, not commit count alone
Reports the bus factor as fragile when one author holds most commits
Does not call 'abandoned' unless commit, release and issue-response stalls all exceed their bars

evals.prompt: We are choosing between two open-source vector databases for production. Which repository is better maintained — contributor spread, release rhythm, unpatched vulnerabilities — before we bet on it?
evals.expected_output: A response that satisfies these checks: Runs the vitality read per repository rather than comparing star counts; Reads contributor concentration, release frequency and open advisories for each; Presents a verdict per repository with the biggest risk, using the output template.
expectations: Runs the vitality read per repository rather than comparing star counts
Reads contributor concentration, release frequency and open advisories for each
